title: Trump Says U.S. Would Enter Iran to Excavate Uranium at Arizona Rally
description_short: At an Arizona rally, Trump said the U.S. would go into Iran to excavate uranium, according to AP’s video headline.
description_medium: At a Turning Point USA rally in Arizona, Trump spoke about the Iran war and said the United States would go into Iran to excavate uranium, according to AP’s video headline. AP’s description says he suggested Iran had agreed to hand over enriched uranium. NPR’s transcript reports cheers during his Iran remarks and attributes a record-low 39% approval rating to an average of polls.
description_long: President Donald Trump spoke at a Turning Point USA campaign-style rally in Arizona in April 2026, during a trip NPR described as an effort to build Republican support in battleground states before the midterm elections. NPR’s transcript places the appearance amid public opposition to the war in Iran and quotes Trump saying the United States had been defending Americans because Iran could not have a nuclear weapon; the report says the crowd cheered during that passage. The Associated Press video headline says Trump said the United States would go into Iran and excavate uranium, while the AP description says he suggested Iran had agreed to hand over enriched uranium. NPR also reports that an average of polls put Trump’s approval at 39%, described as a record low. The material supports an attributed account of these remarks and the event context. It does not establish that Iran agreed to transfer uranium, that the United States carried out an excavation or retrieval operation, or that the statement became policy.

supports: NPR published a recap dated April 18, 2026, describing Trump’s Arizona appearance at a campaign-style Turning Point USA event.
The report describes the crowd as friendly and says it cheered Trump’s remarks about the Iran war.
NPR reports an average of polls put Trump’s approval rating at a record-low 39%; it does not identify the component polls in the article.
limitations: The recap does not provide a complete transcript of Trump’s speech or identify the component polls.

supports: NPR’s transcript says Trump went to Arizona for a campaign-style rally with Turning Point USA.

NPR quotes Trump: ‘We are not ashamed of American might, and we do not hesitate to defend the American people, which is what we’ve been doing for the last two months because Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon.’
The transcript says the crowd cheered during that Iran passage.
NPR reports: ‘In an average of the polls, the president has hit a record low approval rating of 39%.’ It does not name the polls, survey dates, or question wording.
NPR describes Trump’s stated campaign purpose as seeking support in battleground states before the midterms.
limitations: This is an edited broadcast transcript excerpt, not a full transcript of the rally speech.

supports: AP’s video headline reads ‘Trump says US will go into Iran and excavate uranium.’
AP’s page description says Trump suggested in an Arizona speech that Iran had agreed to hand over its enriched uranium.
limitations: The accessible page supplies its headline and description, not a transcript; it does not establish an actual Iranian agreement, U.S. operation, or resulting policy.

rationale: Pass is limited to the supplied reporting and NPR’s linked transcript. Proposed factual corrections: replace the earlier editorialized title and copy with a sourced account of the rally and attributed Iran/uranium remarks; retain the approval claim only as NPR’s report of a 39% average-of-polls figure; remove the unsupported framing of a detailed operational plan, an established Iranian agreement, and the original characterization of the speech as ‘rally delusion’ or as blending war, grievance, and fantasy. The available NPR transcript is not the full rally speech, and the component polls are unnamed; the proposal does not make claims requiring those missing details.
